findings.title: `b2_lifecycle.sh` merges stderr into the JSON it parses
findings.description: `RULES=$(RCLONE_B2_ACCOUNT=... rclone backend lifecycle ":b2:$BUCKET" 2>&1)` captures stderr into the same variable that is then parsed as JSON. `jq -e 'type == "array"'` runs on that merged output, so any rclone warning on stderr (a NOTICE, a deprecation warning, a partial read) makes the JSON invalid and the script reports `UNREADABLE` even though the bucket's rules are readable. The read-only path is a false negative: `--check` would report "unreadable" instead of "missing". The stderr should be captured separately (e.g. `RULES=$(... 2>err)` with the error text only used for the failure message).

findings.title: `UNREADABLE` output from `b2_lifecycle.sh` is not tallied or prefixed by `run_lib`
findings.description: `b2_lifecycle.sh` prints `UNREADABLE lifecycle ...` and exits 1 on the read-failure path. `run_lib`'s prefix regex only matches `OK|DRIFT|MISSING|APPLIED|PENDING RESTART|INFO`, and its `NOT_OK` tally only matches `^(DRIFT|MISSING|PENDING RESTART) `. So an `UNREADABLE` line is printed raw and is not counted, meaning `--check` would exit 0 on an unreadable lifecycle. The test `test_unreadable_rules_are_a_failure` expects `MISSING 17/tick lifecycle-read (rclone backend lifecycle ...`, so the caller must convert `UNREADABLE` to `MISSING <cluster> lifecycle-read ...` — that conversion is not in the visible diff. I could not verify the per-cluster step in `setup-backup.sh` (the hunk stops at the `run_lib` change), so this is a possible mismatch rather than a confirmed one; confirm the caller's conversion before merging.

findings.title: `render_cron.sh` `CLUSTER_TEXT=$(grep -v '^##' ...)` aborts silently on a comment-only template
findings.description: `CLUSTER_TEXT=$(grep -v '^##' "$CLUSTER_TEMPLATE")` runs under `set -euo pipefail`. `grep -v` exits 1 when every line is filtered out, so a template that is all `##` comments (or a template with a trailing newline only) makes the assignment fail and the script exits 1 with no message — the caller's `die "cluster table rejected"` is not reached. The `grep -qx "$CLUSTER_BLOCKS_MARKER"` check only covers the host template. Add a readable guard or a `|| true` on the `grep -v` with a subsequent emptiness check.

findings.title: `die` in `b2_lifecycle.sh` includes the exit code in the message
findings.description: `die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }` is called as `die "unknown argument: $1" 2`, so `$*` includes the trailing `2` and the message reads `error: unknown argument: --foo 2`. The same pattern is pre-existing in `render_cron.sh` and `setup-backup.sh`, so it is consistent with the repo — but the new file propagates it. A two-argument form (`die() { local msg=$1 status=${2:-1}; echo "error: $msg" >&2; exit "$status"; }`) would fix it.

findings.title: `run_lib`'s `sed` prefix is not escaped
findings.description: `run_lib` builds `sed -E "s#^(OK|DRIFT|MISSING|APPLIED|PENDING RESTART|INFO) #\1 $prefix #"` with the cluster name interpolated into the replacement. `$prefix` is currently `17/tick`/`17/main`, which are safe, but a cluster name containing `#`, `&`, or `\` would break the `sed` or expand unexpectedly. Cluster names come from `backup-clusters.conf` and are not validated against those characters. Escaping the prefix or using `sed -E "s#^#... #"` with a fixed prefix would be safer.

findings.title: `run_lib`'s `rc` variable is dead
findings.description: `run_lib() { local prefix=$1 out rc=0; shift; out=$("$@" 2>&1) || rc=$?; ... }` — `rc` is assigned but never read; the `||` only exists to keep `set -e` from exiting. The `rc` variable is dead weight and could be removed or used to log the failing command's status.

findings.title: `ROOT_OF` copy vs `BC_ROOT` — unverified
findings.description: `ROOT_OF=("${BC_ROOT[@]}")` copies the table's roots, and the rehearse block remaps only `ROOT_OF`, leaving `BC_ROOT` at its original values. If the `render_cron.sh` call (not visible in the diff) reads `BC_ROOT` or `--cluster-root` rather than `ROOT_OF`, the rehearse paths would not apply and the rendered cron.d would name the real production roots. I could not verify the call site in the diff; confirm the `render_cron.sh` invocation passes `ROOT_OF`, not `BC_ROOT`.
